first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the observed completion decline and is the most likely single intervention to improve durable activation and time-to-value, which supports sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is highly consequential given the competitor move, but its reported acquisition lift may not translate to durable, qualified revenue after discounting; verify it before prioritizing it. Verify the onboarding result as well because it is the central basis for the intended action and prior evidence emphasizes early adoption rather than downstream qualified revenue.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior result directly addresses the 4% completion decline and showed +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention, making it the strongest available evidence for sustainable revenue improvement. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified acquisition and qualified-revenue lift was offset by a 12% retention decline and failure to survive the first renewal cycle. Measure qualified revenue and retention beyond 30 days because their downstream response remains uncertain.
